title: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1 Is Now Titled 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'
excerpt: Sony Pictures announced the official title on September 28 with a new poster, confirming a worldwide IMAX 3D release on November 6, 2026, in Hindi and English under the tagline "Mankind's greatest story comes to life."
body:
• Nitesh Tiwari's "Ramayana: Part 1" now has an official title: "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend," announced by Sony Pictures on September 28, Ranbir Kapoor's birthday.
  • The film is confirmed for a worldwide release on November 6, 2026, in IMAX and premium large formats, in Hindi and English, with 3D touted as "the most immersive 3D cinematic experience ever."
  • The new poster shows Ranbir Kapoor's Lord Rama facing Yash's Ravana, with the tagline "Mankind's greatest story comes to life."
  • The announcement was made under the #FilmedForIMAX program, and the film's VFX team is credited as being "from the visual artists behind The Odyssey and Dune."

The first part of Nitesh Tiwari's two-part adaptation of the Indian epic finally has an official name. Sony Pictures announced on September 28 — lead actor Ranbir Kapoor's birthday — that "Ramayana: Part 1" is now titled "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend," locking in the film's title, release formats and a new tagline.

The studio unveiled a new poster confirming the title alongside the tagline "Mankind's greatest story comes to life." The poster, according to reports from The Hollywood Reporter India and Variety India, carries the same key visual as previously released — Kapoor's Lord Rama facing Yash's Ravana — and confirms what the makers had long teased: the film is a #FilmedForIMAX release, arriving worldwide on November 6, 2026, in IMAX and premium large formats, in both Hindi and English.

"From the visual artists behind The Odyssey and Dune comes RAMAYANA: RISE OF A LEGEND — the most immersive 3D cinematic experience ever — exclusively in theatres, in IMAX and Premium Large Formats worldwide November 6."

— Sony Pictures, on X

Context & Background

The announcement caps months of build-up. The first full trailer was unveiled on July 30 at 4.15 a.m. during the Brahma Muhurat, introducing the central conflict between Lord Ram and Ravana and showcasing the film's expansive mythological world. A "This Is Our Rama" behind-the-scenes video released alongside the new poster shows Kapoor's transformation into Lord Rama, with Kapoor, director Nitesh Tiwari and veteran actor Arun Govil (who plays King Dasharath) discussing what makes the actor suited to the revered role.

"Lord Rama's biggest strength is not his bow, it is his Kshama (forgiving nature) — his ability to forgive," Kapoor says in the video. "Ye role nahi hai. It's not as if I was offered a film and the role is exciting. It's a responsibility."

The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman and Sunny Deol as Hanuman, with music by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer. It is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in association with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, and Sony Pictures is handling global distribution excluding India. T-Series has locked the music rights for a reported ₹75 crore advance.

Impact & Analysis

The official title and IMAX branding remove any remaining doubt about the film's scale of ambition. An official title — rather than the working "Part 1" label — signals that the franchise is being positioned as a global property in the mould of "The Odyssey" and "Dune," both of which Sony name-dropped in its announcement. The emphasis on "the most immersive 3D cinematic experience ever" is a direct play for the premium-format audience that has driven record weekends for tentpole films worldwide.

The timing is no accident either: the announcement landed on Kapoor's birthday, maximizing fan attention, and comes just days after the star-studded Mumbai promotional event that featured MrBeast — part of a global outreach strategy that has taken the film's marketing from Delhi's Pratham Sankalp event to international stages.

Competition is already lined up. Tamil superstar Suriya's cop thriller "Scene," directed by Jithu Madhavan, releases on the same November 6 date, setting up a high-stakes Diwali box-office clash — though "Ramayana" is expected to dominate screen allocation nationally.

Diaspora Angle

Diaspora audiences are a core part of the plan. With an English-language version, a global IMAX release and Sony's international distribution muscle, "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend" is explicitly engineered to play in Los Angeles, London, Toronto and Sydney as much as in Mumbai and Delhi. For second- and third-generation viewers abroad, it may be their first encounter with the epic on the biggest screen available.

What's Next

"Ramayana: Rise of a Legend" opens worldwide on November 6, 2026, with the domestic Indian release reportedly set for November 8, coinciding with Diwali celebrations. The second part is scheduled for Diwali 2027. With advance bookings still weeks away, the next marker to watch is whether the film's pre-release numbers challenge the biggest Diwali openers — some trade reports already project a Hindi opening of ₹65–85 crore, which would dislodge long-standing records.
